claims.statement: 387 batteries and 310705 samples cover four datasets with diverse chemistries/protocols
55 XJTU cells have six protocol-dependent degradation trajectory groups
Short pre-full-charge current/voltage windows support generally applicable features
Feature-SOH correlation pattern may depend more on chemistry than protocol
claims.evidence_level: author natural conjecture; not causal identification

claims.statement: PINN has smallest regular estimation error in most settings
claims.caveat: Published HUST CNN MAPE 0.0074 is lower than PINN 0.0078

claims.statement: PINN is more stable across tasks and metrics
claims.evidence_level: repeat-distribution comparison, no reported significance test

claims.statement: PINN inference F and MLP have same structure and parameter count; CNN similar; CPU inference timing is reported
claims.evidence_level: architectural fairness and CPU runtime benchmark
claims.caveat: PINN training includes G; hardware and software differ from paper benchmark

claims.statement: PINN performs best in the tested small-sample settings
Performance generally improves as more training batteries are used
claims.caveat: Not strictly monotonic at every published point

claims.statement: One-battery PINN can approach MLP/CNN using three or four batteries
All six XJTU batches have three-model small-sample results for one to four batteries, ten repeats
claims.evidence_level: confirmed 720 XJTU small-sample runs; 120 overlap main batch1

claims.statement: Fine-tuning with frozen G improves on source-only target evaluation
One target battery plus pretraining can outperform one target battery from scratch
For XJTU/TJU, one-battery fine-tuning may outperform two-battery target-only training
claims.caveat: Report every direction; not all directions necessarily satisfy a broad paraphrase

claims.statement: Same-chemistry transfer directions appear more promising
Overall reported MAPE is 0.87 percent
claims.caveat: Four reported dataset percentages 0.85,1.21,0.65,0.78 average to 0.8725; exact overall weighting formula not provided

claims.statement: Data, PDE and monotonicity losses define the proposed PINN
claims.evidence_level: method specification, not an ablation result

claims.statement: G contains transferable degradation dynamics
claims.evidence_level: transfer performance supports usefulness; does not establish physical identifiability

claims.statement: Feature selection and cross-battery testing are intended to avoid leakage
claims.evidence_level: design rationale, no independent leakage control experiment

claims.statement: First-order derivatives balance accuracy and computational complexity
claims.evidence_level: implementation choice; no derivative-order comparison in main PDF

claims.statement: Physical knowledge helps models learn better and faster and may support BMS development
claims.evidence_level: broad discussion; no independent wall-clock or deployed-BMS experiment in main PDF
claims.caveat: Scheduler throughput is not evidence for the paper's model-learning speed claim

split.quote_summary: Select independent test batteries; for remaining batteries shuffle all cycle data and allocate20percent validation, remaining training

physical_meaning.summary: Authors explicitly do not model internal physical/chemical changes or chemical boundary conditions; use initial capacity condition and degradation monotonicity

feature_selection.summary: Authors explicitly refrained from feature selection; all16 retained based on generality/noise/interaction arguments, not feature-ablation evidence

chemical_correlation.summary: Qualitative current/voltage curve explanation and conjecture; deeper chemical causes beyond study scope

leakage.summary: Reviewer reiterated possible task/data mismatch leakage; authors supplied design reasoning and discussion, no universal leakage test or separate controlled experiment
